title: different worlds
aim: Explore future technology, nature, unusual lifestyles and time travel through accurate speculation.
objectives: Discuss future uses of technology with accurate probability language
Use quantifiers to talk about nature and city life
Speculate about unusual lives and degrees of certainty
Write a for-and-against essay and a competition entry

lessons.title: Real or virtual?
goals: Read two opposing views about the future of virtual reality
Use a range of structures for future probability
Make accurate predictions about life in 2040

grammar.title: Future probability
grammar.shortAr: will وgoing to وlikely / unlikely / certain / due to للتكهن، وmight / could للاحتمال.
points: Use will / won't + infinitive without to for predictions based on opinion.
Use be going to when present evidence supports a prediction; use be certain to and be likely / unlikely to for degrees of probability.
Use might, may and could + infinitive without to for possible but uncertain future events.
Use be due to when something is scheduled to happen.
table: Opinion prediction
VR won't replace real holidays anytime soon.
Present evidence
It's going to rain; look at those clouds.
High probability
VR is certain to become more common. / It is likely to be used in travel.
Possible event
VR might replace some kinds of tourism.
Scheduled event
The new headsets are due to go on sale next week.
exceptions: Use probably won't, not won't probably: We probably won't come.
For negative future possibilities use might not or may not, not could not.

vocab.example: A researcher finds out information by reading and talking to people.
Virtual reality can feel almost like real life.
Smart technology is controlled by computers.
The researchers published their findings after the study.
The tech industry is spending a lot on VR.
Many people can now work remotely from anywhere.
We need to analyse the information before we predict results.
It is difficult to predict the future of technology.

reading.summary: The article presents two views of VR: supporters see value in education, training, health and low-impact travel, while critics question the cost, evidence and ability to replace real experience.

listening.summary: Vocabulary bank: word families for science and technology.
Pronunciation: connected speech in phrases about future probability.

video.summary: Speakers describe the impact of social media on their daily lives.

speaking: Decide whether predictions about offices, universities, concerts and medicine will happen, might happen or definitely won't happen.
Discuss how accurate your predictions are and what other uses VR might have by 2040.
writing: Write a short prediction paragraph about VR in 2040 using at least four different future probability structures.

practice.q: The critic in the article says VR ___ replace real-life training.
practice.why: The writer argues that virtual practice cannot replace real practice.

practice.q: Look at those black clouds! It ___ rain.
practice.why: be going to is used when there is clear present evidence.

practice.q: The training session ___ start at 9 a.m.
practice.why: be due to describes something scheduled to happen.

practice.q: After arranging scientific tests, researchers publish their ___.
practice.why: Findings are the results of research.

lessons.title: Closer to nature
goals: Understand a radio programme about the benefits of nature
Use quantifiers with singular, plural and uncountable nouns

grammar.title: Quantifiers
grammar.shortAr: تُستخدم الكمّيات حسب نوع الاسم: جمع، لا معدود، أو مفرد؛ a few / a little كمية صغيرة، few /little أقل من المطلوب.
points: Use several, few, a few and a handful of with plural countable nouns.
Use the majority of, a lack of and no with plural or uncountable nouns; use each and every with singular nouns.
Use very little, a little and a good deal of with uncountable nouns.
table: Plural countable
Several of us try to find time outdoors.
Large amount
I spend a good deal of time commuting.
Not enough / none
There is a lack of green public spaces. / We have no time to spare.
Singular
Each time you do this, you'll feel more relaxed.
Small amount
Take a few moments or a handful of plants.
exceptions: a few and a little suggest a small positive amount; few and little suggest less than we want.
In a majority and in a minority describe people or things rather than a noun after the phrase.

vocab.example: The wild coastline has long beaches and cliffs.
We walked on a deserted beach after midnight.
The city needs more open space for families.
They sat on the river bank and watched the water.
The mountain scenery is spectacular.
Morning sunlight came through the trees.
A narrow track led down to the river.
The woodland is quiet early in the morning.

reading.summary: A short text explains that about two hours a week in nature can improve well-being, whether on a wild coastline, in woodland or beside a river.

listening.summary: Radio programme: why time in nature can restore balance and improve well-being.
Pronunciation: linking inside quantifiers such as the majority of.
Pronunciation practice: connected speech in a good deal of, a lack of and in a minority.

speaking: Suggest ways for your school or college to encourage time in nature, including green spaces, events and schedules.
Refocus the group when discussion gets stuck and agree on five practical suggestions.
writing: Write a 180–200 word for-and-against essay about living in the countryside, using contrast linkers and a clear conclusion.

practice.q: There is ___ green public space in many big cities.
practice.why: a lack of means there is not enough of something.

practice.q: ___ students in our class go outside at lunchtime; only four of us do.
practice.why: a handful of means a small number.

practice.q: I spend ___ time commuting every day.
practice.why: time is uncountable, so a good deal of is appropriate.

practice.q: The land beside a river is called the ___.
practice.why: A river bank is the land along the side of a river.

lessons.title: Amazing lives
goals: Read about three women with extreme lifestyles
Speculate using phrases that show how certain you are
Stress the words that signal certainty in speech

grammar.title: How to speculate
grammar.shortAr: للتكهن نستخدم I reckon / I suppose / I'd guess، ولليقين I know for a fact أو bound to.
points: Use I'd guess, I'd have thought, I'd imagine, I suppose and I reckon to give an opinion.
Use I get the impression that, clearly, obviously and bound to when evidence supports your guess.
Use There's no way for ideas you think are impossible and I know for a fact for total certainty.
table: General guess
I'd guess it must be inspiring to see the world like that.
Opinion
I reckon life on the Space Station must be a bit boring.
Based on evidence
I get the impression that she enjoys being alone.
Strong prediction
She's bound to feel scared sometimes.
Impossible
There's no way I would ever consider doing that.
Certain fact
I know for a fact that being at sea alone is not easy.
exceptions: I know for a fact signals 100 percent certainty; There's no way signals impossibility.
Stress the words that carry the speaker's level of certainty.

vocab.example: Her lifestyle is unique; nobody else lives like her.
She lives a modest life on a small boat.
Life in space can make ordinary tasks difficult.
He had a fulfilling career as an astronaut.
Life on the station can be tedious at times.
Running around the world can be exhausting.
The long journey was difficult but rewarding.
She faced harsh winters and loneliness.

reading.summary: The article profiles a marine nomad, an astronaut and a solo runner, showing how unusual lives can be both rewarding and difficult.

listening.summary: Conversation about a TV series, speculating about Karen Nyberg and Rosie Swale-Pope.
Mediation bank model: note taking and summarising an informal interview.
Mediation bank practice: summarising key points from an informal interview.

speaking: Choose four famous people and discuss what they enjoy about life and how they feel about fame.
Speculate about why they might sometimes be unhappy and decide whose life sounds best.
writing: Write six sentences about an unusual lifestyle using at least four different speculation phrases.

practice.q: Which phrase shows the strongest certainty?
options: I know for a fact that …
practice.answer: I know for a fact that …
practice.why: This phrase says the speaker is completely sure.

practice.q: Which phrase says something is impossible?
options: There's no way I'd ever do that.
practice.answer: There's no way I'd ever do that.

practice.q: Life on the road can be ___ but also incredibly rewarding.
practice.why: The article describes the physical challenge of the journey as exhausting.

practice.q: A lifestyle that is completely different from most people's is ___.
practice.why: Unique means unlike anyone or anything else.

lessons.title: The time traveller
goals: Understand a Doctor Who episode about Vincent van Gogh
Recognise extreme adjectives and signpost a sequence of ideas
Plan an imaginary trip back in time and write a competition entry

grammar.title: Signposting an imaginary trip
grammar.shortAr: نظّم الرحلة بعبارات مثل To start with وAnother possibility would be وAnd last but not least.
points: Use To start with and With that in mind to organise the opening of a plan.
Use What else? and Another possibility would be to introduce a new idea.
Use And last but not least for the final point.
table: Start the plan
To start with, I'd go to the nineteenth century.
Refer back
With that in mind, I'd visit a café in Paris.
Add an idea
What else? Another possibility would be to meet the artist.
Finish the sequence
And last but not least, I'd bring back a painting.
Extreme adjective
The final months were an astonishing artistic outpouring.
exceptions: Extreme adjectives such as astonishing and magnificent already mean very; use very fine, not very magnificent.
With that in mind refers to something that has just been said.

vocab.example: The number of paintings was astonishing.
The colours in the painting are incredible.
These paintings are precious and must be protected.
The museum is a mighty building in Paris.
Van Gogh is often called the finest painter of them all.
His command of colour was magnificent.
The museum holds many of the greatest paintings in history.

reading.summary: The programme notes introduce Doctor Who and Vincent van Gogh, an artist whose work became famous only after his difficult and largely unrecognised life.

listening.summary: Pronunciation practice: stressing the words that show how certain a speaker is.
A speaker explains an imaginary trip back in time and organises it with key phrases.
Review listening: solitude, quantifiers and future probability in context.

video.summary: In this Doctor Who episode, the Doctor and Amy travel back to meet van Gogh and learn how his work will later be valued.

speaking: Plan where and when you would travel, who you would meet and what you would do.
Present your trip back in time using clear signposting phrases and explain why it would be exciting.
writing: Write a competition entry about an imaginary journey through time, using extreme adjectives and clear sequencing.

practice.q: The extreme adjective meaning very surprising or amazing is ___.
Which phrase introduces the final item in a sequence?
options: And last but not least, I'd …
practice.answer: And last but not least, I'd …
practice.why: This phrase signals the last point in a plan.

practice.q: The museum is home to many of the ___ paintings in history.
practice.why: Greatest means best or most important.

practice.q: Which adjective means best in the phrase the ___ painter of them all?
practice.why: Finest means of the highest quality.

review.summary: Recycle future probability, quantifiers, speculation, nature and lifestyle vocabulary, plus language for time travel.
tasks: Complete the solitude text with quantifiers and probability forms, then check your answers with R2.
Write five accurate predictions about future holidays or technology using at least three different structures.
Speculate about an unusual life using three different levels of certainty.

The train is ___ depart at 6 p.m.
We ___ probably visit the virtual exhibition tomorrow.
There ___ green public spaces in many city centres.
___ people in major cities use public transport.
I spend ___ time outdoors than I used to.

options: I know for a fact that …
quiz.answer: I know for a fact that …

quiz.q: Which phrase means something is impossible?
A person who finds out information by reading and speaking to people is a ___.
An area of land with a lot of trees is ___.
A simple lifestyle that does not cost much is ___.
The extreme adjective for very large and important is ___.
What does the VR article say about virtual forests?
options: They may reduce stress as much as real forests.
They are more expensive than real forests.
There is no evidence about them.
quiz.answer: They may reduce stress as much as real forests.

quiz.q: What happened to van Gogh's reputation after he died?
options: His work became popular and he is now famous.
quiz.answer: His work became popular and he is now famous.
